rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests Quraysh and others by granting worldly ease; they mistake this for divine favor and look down on poor believers, though meeting the Prophet itself tests whether they act well or badly.
rows.anchor: فغرهم ذلك وظنوا أنهم أحباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The testing may also refer to the famine the Prophet invoked against Mecca; even after eating carrion, its people did not repent.
rows.anchor: أو كان ابتلاؤنا لهم بالقحط الذي دعا عليهم به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أكلوا الجيف فما تابوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famous orchard lay near Sanaa at al-Darwan; its owner customarily left fallen or missed fruit for the poor, but his sons resolved to harvest before sunrise so no poor person could claim any.
rows.anchor: كان صاحبه ينادي الفقراء وقت الصرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression for cutting the orchard conveys a decisive, complete severing that would prevent the poor from sharing its fruit.
rows.anchor: عبر به عن الجذاذ بدلالته على القطع البائن المعزوم عليه المستأثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not making an exception means they neither said inshallah nor used another phrase returning the matter to God's will; such an exception removes some of the oath's absolute force.
rows.anchor: لا يطلبون ولا يوجدون ثنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroying visitor is a slight act for God though devastating to the orchard; the phrase from your Lord frames the punishment as merciful correction intended to reform the Prophet's people.
rows.anchor: عذاب مهلك محيط مع أنه أمر يسير جدا عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although it is said that a taif in this sense must occur at night, the author rejects that restriction by citing a taif from Satan that touches people.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون الطائف بهذا المعنى إلا بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sarim can mean trees stripped of fruit, something severed from its destination, a dark night, or black ash; the orchard was entirely ruined because the heirs sought everything and did not give charity.
rows.anchor: كالأشجار التي صرم عنها ثمرها أو كالشيء الذي انقطع ما بينه وبين قاصده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their resolve made them act as if they had arranged a meeting: they called to one another at the first part of morning.
rows.anchor: لقوة عزمهم على ما أقسموا عليه كأنهم كانوا على ميعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They urged one another to go very early to their cultivated orchard, the place from which they expected benefit and which they regarded as theirs alone.
rows.anchor: بكروا جدا مقبلين ومستولين وقادرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling themselves harvesters can mean those cutting the crop or those firmly resolved to cut it without sharing it.
rows.anchor: جاذين جذاذا ليسلم لكم من غير مشاركة أحد لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They set out promptly and whispered like people planning a theft; takhafut derives from quietness or stillness.
rows.anchor: يقولون في حال انطلاقهم قولا هو في غاية السر كأنهم ذاهبون إلى سرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is phrased as barring a poor person from entering, but rhetorically they are forbidding themselves from letting one in; they intend to search throughout the day so none can reach fruit or an opening.
rows.anchor: وهو نهي للمسكين في اللفظ للمبالغة في نهي أنفسهم أن لا يدعوه يدخل عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥard can mean aim, intense anger, firm insistence, haste, stinginess, or lack of good, as in a season without rain or a camel withholding milk.
rows.anchor: وهو القصد وشدة الغضب مع الجزم بالأمر واللجاج فيه والسرعة والنكد بالمنع وقلة الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They thought themselves capable of harvesting because they had made no exception; such certainty about a future act presumes a power no creature has.
rows.anchor: عند أنفسهم وفي زعمهم بدليل عدم استثنائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a short walk they saw no trace of crop or fruit and first assumed they had lost their way, because the destroyed orchard bore no resemblance to the one they knew.
rows.anchor: بعد سير يسير وليس للزرع ولا للثمر بها أثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They then recognized that they were deprived of the expected good because God took it in response to their intention to deprive the poor; God does not change a people until they change themselves.
rows.anchor: الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A calamity softens and leads to repentance for one whom God intends to guide, but increases another person's disbelief.
rows.anchor: وما كان القرع بالمصائب مظنة الرقة والتوبة لمن أريد به الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their middle brother was superior in judgment, reason, age, leadership, and virtue, and had warned them that their plan was improper.
rows.anchor: أي رأيا وعقلا وسنا ورئاسة وفضلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By asking why they did not glorify God, the brother means they should have denied that their plan could override God's will; at minimum they should have said inshallah when swearing.
rows.anchor: وأقل التسبيح الاستثناء عند الإقسام شكا في قدرة الإنسان وإثباتا لقدرة الملك الديان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They immediately repent, declaring God free of injustice and confessing entrenched wrongdoing: they withheld their father's charity and swore without referring the outcome to God.
rows.anchor: تنزه المحسن إلينا التنزيه الأعظم عن أن يكون وقع منه فيما فعل بنا ظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn on one another in mutual reproach; the equal wording for both sides signals that all share in the repentance and blame.
rows.anchor: ودلت التسوية بين فريقيهم في اللفظ على الاستواء في التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is to establish the Resurrection, warn its deniers, portray its magnitude through the greatness of its King and the length of its day, and console the Prophet for the humiliation awaiting rejecters.
rows.anchor: إثبات القيامة وأنذار من كفر بها وتصوير عظمتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Haqqah at the end of the preceding surah already signals that the Resurrection must occur; this surah continues the proof through divine power, knowledge, and God's transcendence above the defect of neglect.
rows.anchor: ودل على وجوب وقوعها سابقا بما ختمه بتسميتها في السورة الماضية بالحاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah continues a Quran-wide warning about resurrection: Noah was the earliest messenger sent to warn his people, while Muhammad is the last; the jinn too were warned about it.
rows.anchor: فأرسل نوحا عليه السلام يفي الزمان الأقدم كما ذكر في سورته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names Saʾala and al-Maʿarij best signal the surah's purpose; the event is near, so the specially faithful should prepare before no refuge remains.
rows.anchor: وكذا المعارج وهما أنسب ما فيها للدلالة على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the ransom scene the farthest source of benefit or harm is named first; unlike the escape scene in 80:34, that passage names the closest people first.
rows.anchor: قدم الأبعد عن ذلك فالأبعد من جهة النفع والمعرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase everyone on earth includes both jinn and humans, whether or not the person is an intimate companion, and jamiʿa confirms that min is truly universal.
rows.anchor: من الثقلين وغيرهم سواء كان فيهم صديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since people will see everything clearly and know nothing can rescue them from their overwhelming sins, then marks their wish for a rescue renewed at some future time, which is impossible.
rows.anchor: يعلم أنه لا ينجيه من الخطايا المحيطة المحبطة شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla decisively rebukes the criminal's wish: no ransom or imagined hope will ever produce escape.
rows.anchor: ليكن للمجرم ردع أي ردع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laza is a fire with pure, extreme flame that consumes itself when it finds nothing else to consume and devours whatever it finds.
rows.anchor: ذات اللهب الخالص المتناهي في الحر يتلظى أي يتوقد فيأكل بسببه بعضها بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shawa is explained as the skin of the head, hands, feet, extremities, or skull; another view includes all skin and flesh, stripped and then restored so the condemned repeatedly feel the punishment.
rows.anchor: اليدان والرجلان والأطراف وقحف الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire's calling may be metaphorical for drawing sinners to it or literal speech summoning a polytheist or hypocrite before it catches them like birds picking grain.
rows.anchor: إلي يا مشرك إلي يا منافق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It summons anyone who turned away from the truth or from deeds that could save them; turning away means deliberately making one's original sound nature reject the path of salvation.
rows.anchor: من وقع منه إدبارهما من حقه الإقبال عليه سواء كان ذلك الإدبار عنها أو عن الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this world and the next are rivals, turning toward one entails turning away from the other; the condemned gathered worldly things and hoarded them instead of paying God's due.
rows.anchor: فكان الإقبال على إحداهما دالا على الإعراض عن الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is naturally self-absorbed, admiring itself and forgetting its Lord and sins; it was created with an intense mix of distress, greed, impatience, and miserliness.
rows.anchor: الإنسان مقهور مع جبلته إلا من حفظه الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains haluʿ as being greedy for what is unlawful; another report from him says the following two clauses explain the word.
rows.anchor: أنه الحريص على ما لا يحل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When even slight harm touches a person, the haluʿ person falls into extreme distress, the opposite of patience.
rows.anchor: ضد الصبر بحث يكاد صاحبه ينقد نصفين ويتفتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When good or provision touches a person, the haluʿ person withholds required rights because love of immediate gain narrows his view; this is the opposite of faith.
rows.anchor: في حب العاجل وقصور النظر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception identifies those who maintain prayer: their worship restrains the haluʿ nature so that neither their distress nor withholding becomes extreme, and they act to please God.
rows.anchor: لا يشتد هلعهم فلا يشتد جزعهم ولا منعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God equips them to refine their nature through good companions, admonition, avoiding corrupt places and company, and habits that prompt noble conduct; preserving religious limits despite contrary impulses is a great honor.
rows.anchor: من أصدقاء الخير وأولياء المعروف وسماع المواعظ الحسان والإبعاد عن معادن الدنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight qualities that follow correspond to the eight gates of Paradise and complete faith's two halves, patience and gratitude.
rows.anchor: لما جمع من هذه الأوصاف الثمان المعادة لأبواب الجنة الثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being constant in prayer means no laxity or separation from it; prayer remains before their attention even between performances because it connects them to God.
rows.anchor: لا فتور لهم عنها ولا انفكاك لهم منها بل يلازمونها ملازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word prayer covers all kinds, though obligatory prayer is chiefly intended; prayer has conditions, pillars, supplementary acts, forms, and etiquette, and may include bowing and prostration, prostration alone, or neither as in the funeral prayer.
rows.anchor: والمراد الجنس الشامل لجميع الأنواع إلا أن معظم المقصود الفرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He pivots from purification of the soul through prayer to purification of its counterpart, wealth; because this context is broader than the benefactors in al-Dhariyat, he focuses on obligatory dues.
rows.anchor: السياق هنا لأعم من المحسنين الذين تقدموا في الذاريات اقتصر على الفرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is to show the Prophet's honor: God softened the hearts of humans, jinn, and others toward him, his companions, and his household, through the Quran's extraordinary character.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إظهار الشرف لهذا النبي الكريم الفاتح صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's time among his people was less than a tenth of Noah's, though Noah's people had largely rejected him; the surah's names, al-Jinn and Qul Uhiya, point to its subject.
rows.anchor: والزمان في آخره وزمان لبثه في قومه دون ربع العشر من زمن نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is unsurprising when a servant calls upon and devotes himself to his own Master; the real cause for amazement is worshipping another or inclining even slightly toward another.
rows.anchor: إنما يعجب ممن دعا غير سيده أو مال إليه أدنى ميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening may mean God revealed that when Muhammad stood in prayer the jinn nearly crowded over him, or may be the jinn recounting to their people what they saw of his prayer and his companions' gathering around him.
rows.anchor: أوحي إلي أو قال الجن لمن أطاعهم من قومهم حاكين ما رأوا من صلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Muhammad God's servant highlights that he worships the supreme King; even a servant of the least master would not be treated this way, much less the King of kings.
rows.anchor: فكيف إذا كان سيده مالك الملك وملك الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent setting is Muhammad praying in the valley of Nakhlah, where jinn sent toward Tihamah by Iblis saw him, crowded close, heard the Quran and his monotheism, and believed.
rows.anchor: لما قمت في الصلاة أعبد الله في بطن نخلة ورآني الجن الذي وجههم إبليس نحو تهامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Saʿid ibn Jubayr are also reported to interpret the passage as the jinn telling their people about the Prophet's prayer and the companions standing closely around him to pray and learn.
rows.anchor: ويحكى هذا القول عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An envoy sent by the Persian king described Muslims praying in orderly rows behind one leader, all bowing, prostrating, sitting, and acting together; the king was struck by this and mentioned Umar.
rows.anchor: إذا صلوا صفوا أنفسهم صفوفا ويقدمهم رجل يقومون بقيامة ويسجدون بسجوده

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makhul, as quoted by Abu Hayyan, says seventy thousand followed the Prophet on the night of the jinn and dispersed at daybreak.
rows.anchor: ونقل أبو حيان عن مكحول أنه بلغ من تابع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة الجن سبعين ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet denies worshipping any partner alongside his Lord, including Wadd, Suwaʿ, and Yaghuth, whether an idol or a living being.
rows.anchor: من ود وسواع ويغوث وغيرها من الصامت والناطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot independently bring people harm, benefit, misguidance, or right guidance; Abu Hayyan calls the paired omissions in this phrasing ihtibak.
rows.anchor: فحذف من كل ما يدل مقابله عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عربي الطائي
rows.claim: The author condemns Ibn Arabi al-Ta'i's apparent claim that misguidance is more rightly guided than guidance, arguing its plain meaning conflicts with the verse and Islamic law.
rows.anchor: قبح الله ابن عربي الطائي الذي يقول في فصوصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God intends harm, no one can protect the Prophet from Him; there is no refuge, detour, place of retreat, or stratagem outside God's authority.
rows.anchor: معدلا وموضع ميل وركون ومدخلا وملتجأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Multahad derives from the idea of leaning or turning away from truth toward falsehood.
rows.anchor: لأن اللحد أصله الميل ولا يقال إلا في ميل من حق إلى باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah teaches that excellent deeds avert dangers, lighten burdens, and especially prepare one for standing before God at night; night worship also helps patience through life's troubles, and its title points to this purpose.
rows.anchor: محاسن الأعمال تدفع الأخطار والأوجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to endure the opponents' words anticipates severe trials, while its wording also suggests their attacks reach the Prophet only through speech.
rows.anchor: أمر بها مشيرا إلى أنه لا بد أن يكون عن هذا القول الثقيل خطوب طوال وزلازل وأهوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautifully leaving the deniers means outwardly meeting them when needed while inwardly keeping apart, fulfilling duties such as calling them to God and sharing their joys and sorrows without demanding one's own rights.
rows.anchor: تعاشرهم بظاهرك وتباينهم بسرك وخاطرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells the Prophet to leave the deniers' treatment to Him; their affluence and comfortable lives, especially among Quraysh's leaders, are what made worldly attachment a danger.
rows.anchor: أصحاب التنعم بغضارة العيش والبهجة التي أفادتهموها النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should let them be for a short time, patiently and gradually, without worrying over their eventual punishment.
rows.anchor: اتركهم برفق وتأن وتدريج ولا تهتم بشأنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time between this warning and Badr was short, according to Muhibb al-Tabari, promising that the Prophet would outlive his opponents' seizure.
rows.anchor: بين نزول هذه الآية وبين وقعة بدر يسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage directs the Prophet to entrust the opponents to God and devote himself inwardly and outwardly to God; being preoccupied with an enemy can leave a person to himself, while reliance removes that barrier.
rows.anchor: فإذا توكل عليه فقد أزال ذلك المانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankal are heavy, lasting fetters imposed to humiliate those who bound themselves to desires and followed the caller's path only through the open space of caprice.
rows.anchor: القيد الثقيل الذي لايفك أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire contrasts with the opponents' luxurious cooling drinks and fine clothes by giving them fiercely burning Hellfire.
rows.anchor: بما كانوا يتقيدون به من تبريد الشراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choking food may be dariʿ or zaqqum: it catches in the throat and can neither be swallowed nor expelled, contrasting with their refined meals and pursuit of every pleasure.
rows.anchor: لا ينزل ولا يخرج بما كانوا يعانونه من تصفية المآكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general painful punishment removes every remaining sweetness from the lives of those who mocked the call to escape sense-bound desire for enduring good works.
rows.anchor: مؤلما شديد الإيلام لا يدع لهم عذوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is earnest warning to the arrogant about ruin, establishing resurrection even for obstinate deniers, and giving mindful people hope in the Forbearing, Forgiving God; its title points to the opening call.
rows.anchor: الجد والاجتهاد في الإنذار بدار البوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes doubt about the Resurrection's terrors and tells listeners to prepare, since its magnitude surpasses what they can imagine.
rows.anchor: لأن الأمر أطم وأعظم مما يخطر بالبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by the moon, night, and dawn reinforces the warning: the moon guides night travelers, while receding darkness and dawn's light portray knowledge and guidance displacing ignorance and doubt.
rows.anchor: آية الليل الهادية لمن ضل بظلامه

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub allows adbara to mean that dawn approached, citing the Arab phrase meaning that someone came behind me.
rows.anchor: دبرني فلان أي جاء خلفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sunrise analogy depicts knowledge and guidance arriving as dawn illuminates and dispels confusion.
rows.anchor: أقبل ضياؤه بجل العلم بحلوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is one of the greatest calamities, or one of the seven immense levels of Hell; the author lists Jahannam, Lazaa, Hutamah, Saʿir, Saqar, Jahim, and Hawiyah.
rows.anchor: أو المراد بها واحد سبع هي غاية في الكبر أي دركات النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadhir may describe a tremendous warner, the warning conveyed by the fire, or a warning of exceptional force; nadhir can function as an intensive or a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: عظيما أو من جهة نذارتها أو إنذارا بالغا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the warning one for all humanity fits how quickly bodily beings are affected, especially by fire.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم من الإشارة إلى إسراع الجسم العادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People have capacity and choice in their actions, though God creates them and conceals their outcomes, so they are addressed as able to advance toward good or turn away from it.
rows.anchor: خلق في الإنسان قوة واختيارا بها يفعل ما قدره الله له وغطى عنه علم العاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase whoever wills to advance or fall back, the object is omitted because it is understood from common usage; the infinitive clause can be a subject or an apposition shifting from absent people to direct address.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول لأن استعماله كثير حتى صار يعرف وإن لم يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul, male or female, is held by its own deeds rather than another's; rahina means a pawn or pledge, with the Hamasa verse cited as a lexical witness.
rows.anchor: ذكر أو أنثى على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hamasa poet's use of rahina witnesses the meaning of something pledged or held as security; the ending is not feminine agreement for rahin, since that participle's form applies to either gender.
rows.anchor: أبعد الذي بالعنف نعف كويكب رهينة رمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending may intensify the sense of being firmly bound, or rahina may mean doomed, since a pledge can be released or forfeited and most people perish.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الهاء للمبالغة بمعنى موثقة إيثاقا بليغا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right are exempt because they obeyed God's commands and avoided prohibitions; God accepts their good deeds and overlooks their sins.
rows.anchor: الذين تحيزوا إلى الله فائتمروا بأوامره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their place in gardens shows they freed themselves instead of remaining pledged; the wording uses ellipsis by affirming pledge first and Paradise second to imply their opposites.
rows.anchor: أثبت أولا الارتهان دليلا على حذف ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saved ask about criminals from a position of ease, showing that they are free from the worries that burdened them.
rows.anchor: السؤال عن حال الغير دالا دلالة واضحة على الراحة والفراغ عن كل ما يهم النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is to display the majesty of the Prophet commissioned to warn, and of his Sender, through the Quran's clarity, eloquence, sound, and lofty aims; sincere intent and resolve uncover its meanings.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على عظمة المدثر المأمور بالإنذار صلى الله عليه وسلم لعظمة مرسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may conceal the Quran's insights from some and unveil them for others; as the Prophet embodied the Quran, guided followers can memorize, understand, and live its meanings.
rows.anchor: كما كان المدثر صلى الله عليه وسلم حين كان خلقه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening la may negate an oath or reinforce it; the Resurrection is so evident that an oath is unnecessary, since even human authorities supervise their dependents, much more so the Supreme Judge.
rows.anchor: النافية للقسم أو المؤكدة مع أنها في الوضوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels continually take people to the intermediate realm, return them to earth for burial, and then gather them at the trumpet for judgment and reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: ويسوقونهم زمرا بعد زمر إلى العود في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive yunnabbaʾ foregrounds disclosure of hidden deeds rather than who discloses them and emphasizes that the task is easy for God.
rows.anchor: بانيا للمفعول لأن المنكئ إنما هو كشف الأسرار لا كونه من كاشف معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What a person sent ahead and left behind can mean all early and late deeds, preferring law over desire, unfinished acts cut short by death, or deeds personally done versus beneficial or harmful practices others continue; Ibn Abbas holds the last interpretation, followed by al-Ghazali.
rows.anchor: ما سنه فعمل به الناس من بعده من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is an emphatic, clear witness against himself: careful reflection on one's original nature reveals good and bad deeds, while in the afterlife all one's acts become present to memory.
rows.anchor: أي حجة بينة على أعماله

rows.speaker: أبو ثعلبة الخشني
rows.claim: The Prophet's report, narrated by Abu Thaʿlaba al-Khushani and recorded by Ahmad, says righteousness is what reassures the heart, while sin unsettles the breast even if people give a favorable ruling.
rows.anchor: سكنت إليه النفس واطمأن إليه القلب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The Prophet's saying, reported by Ibn Masud and recorded by al-Bukhari, that people retained from earlier prophethood is: if you feel no shame, do as you wish.
rows.anchor: إنما أدرك الناس من كلام النبوة الأولى إذا لم تستح فاصنع ما شئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the afterlife God strengthens memory, removes bodily distraction and spiritual veils, and makes deeds appear as if seen; excuses fail because the person, conditions, or speaking limbs expose their falsehood.
rows.anchor: حتى تصير أعماله ممثلة له كأنه يراها ولا تنفعه معذرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah warns humanity about judgment after all creatures are gathered, with disobedient people punished in fire and obedient people rewarded in gardens amid long, terrifying scenes; its names point to human origin and fate.
rows.anchor: بما دل عليه آخر القيامة من العرض على الملك الديان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names al-Insan, Hal Ata, al-Amshaj, and al-Dahr all signal the surah's central concern with humanity's beginning and end.
rows.anchor: وكذا تسميتها بهل أتى وبالدهر وبالأمشاج من غير ميل ولا اعوجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening rebukes the notion that humanity is left without command or purpose: although people once were not mentioned, after creation they are always significant, and the favored human cannot simply disappear without resurrection.
rows.anchor: ثم يذهب عدما ليس الأمر كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dahr means time, which al-Razi defines as the measure of the celestial sphere's motion; the passage argues that time and creation are ordered with humanity in view, making resurrection fitting.
rows.anchor: والزمان هو مقدار حركة الفلك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says Adam was made from earth and then remained in stages of clay, shaped clay, and altered dark clay for forty years each before being formed after 160 years.
rows.anchor: خلق الله آدم عليه السلام من تراب فأقام أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi quotes Ibn Abbas as saying Adam was formed after 120 years rather than the 160 years attributed to Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: خلقَه بعد عشرين ومائة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man recited the verse before Ibn Masud, who responded, 'I wish that had not been,' expressing dread at humanity's former insignificance.
rows.anchor: يا ليت ذلك لم يكن

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says the verse recalls humanity's humble beginnings to prevent pride and the false belief that divine favors are personally deserved.
rows.anchor: تعريف الإنسان بحاله وابتداء أمره ليعلم أن لا طريق له للكبر واعتقاد السيادة لنفسه
